newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSTANT VIEW - Japan June trade surplus up 27.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Japan June trade surplus up 27.7 pct.

text.p: The following is a selection of economists' and analysts' initial reactions to figures for Japan's June customs-cleared trade surplus, which the government said on Thursday rose 27.7 percent to 934.21 billion yen:
RICHARD JERRAM, CHIEF ECONOMIST, ING BARINGS SECURITIES:

"The surplus has come in quite a long way below market expectations. That bodes quiet well for the dollar in the short term, although what we are looking at is the difference between export and import growth. Exports are still growing quite a bit faster than imports and we think the surplus will continue to increase for some months to come."
TOSHIHIKO MASAKI, SENIOR TRADER, LONG-TERM CREDIT BANK OF JAPAN:

"The dollar was bought (for yen) as the June surplus was at the lower-end of market projections. The amount of the surplus was still significantly large, and that could have put downward pressure on the dollar.

"However, Japan-U.S. trade tension is now being temporarily shelved by the market... Traders may switch their focus back to trade issues within the next few months if U.S. monetary authorities start to complain about Tokyo's persistent surplus."
LARRY DUKE, VICE PRESIDENT, CITIBANK N.A.:

"I think it's a short-term buy on dips (for the dollar). (The dollar) may go up to 117 yen levels. But I agree in the medium term the widening surplus trend is definitely a negative factor for the dollar."

"We think the surplus will grow for another year at the very least and probably for another two years. It's clear that the depreciation of the yen over the last two years is having an impact on the competitiveness of imports and exports.

"And at the same time, this is compounded by very weak domestic demand in Japan. So there is not much demand for buying imports in any case. And that's been hurt by loss of competitiveness (of imports). So in the medium term, the surplus is just going to keep on going up and up."
